rationale: This is simply the numerator sum of two already-tested archive signals with the identical denominator (Acquired Franchise Cash Margin, oancf/(sale+gdwl), and Goodwill Integration Earnings Gain, Δoiadp/(sale+gdwl)), and because the oancf level is an order of magnitude larger than the one-year income change it will be dominated by the archived cash-margin signal rather than testing anything new.

This is the archived Intangible Maintenance Cash Surplus ((oancf−dp)/(sale+intan), fmb 2.22, alpha 0.037) with xrd added to the numerator — a one-term cosmetic variant whose incremental content (R&D intensity, a long-known anomaly) is already well documented and heavily represented elsewhere in the archive.

Near-rediscovery of the archived Goodwill Integration Earnings Gain (Δoiadp/(sale+gdwl)) differing only by adding Δxrd, and the archive already showed that construction yields essentially zero Fama-MacBeth slope (t=0.03), so this variant does not address the diagnosed level-versus-change problem it claims to target.

Mechanical oiadp→oancf substitution inside the already-tested Intangible Pricing-Power Conversion; the dollar margin-change term is small relative to the cash-flow level, so this collapses to a cash profitability ratio very close to several archived cash-margin signals rather than isolating pricing power.

The most structurally original of the batch, but the hypothesis and interaction_type claim conditioning on intangible richness while intan enters only as a denominator penalty (intangible-heavy firms are mechanically pushed lower), and the numerator algebraically reduces to 2·oiadp − sale·lagged-peak-margin, an arbitrary weighting of level profitability against a peak gap that is not motivated.

Adding Δ(ib+xrd) to the archived Organic Intangible Equity Productivity numerator yields roughly 2×current minus lagged earnings over the same denominator, so it is highly collinear with the archived signal and amounts to blending two long-published anomalies (profitability and earnings growth) without a distinct mechanism.
